The main takeaway from our work is that
HRV is a common respiratory virus that is frequently found in lung transplant recipients, and that it is not associated with a higher risk of acute rejection.
HRV infection should be suspected in the presence of clinical symptoms and histopathological evidence of lung involvement, even in the absence of a high viral load.

HRV is a relevant pathogen that may cause lung disease, and that it is important to consider the possibility of HRV infection in the differential diagnosis of lung disease in immunocompromised individuals.
